statusDetail: Homepage was challenged by Cloudflare, but four representative public templates plus login and error recovery were directly audited. Authenticated posting, messaging, checkout/subscription, and account-management internals were not covered because they require an account.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored on public content pages
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated listing screenshot is byte-identical to the light desktop capture and remains white; DOM tokens include dark values but the rendered page stays light.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply the existing dark design tokens from a prefers-color-scheme default unless the user has explicitly selected a stored theme.

findings.summary: Motion is not reduced for users who request it
findings.evidence: The live CSS probe found one active animation and no prefers-reduced-motion rule on the listing surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential transitions and animations in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and provide a reduced alternative.

findings.summary: Automated contrast checks fail
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility reported a failing color-contrast audit on the mobile listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text and control contrast to WCAG AA and verify in forced-colors and prefers-contrast modes.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The rendered CSS probe found no view-transition declarations across the listing SPA surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for tag, tab, and detail navigation while preserving reduced-motion behavior.

findings.summary: Long listing chrome does not communicate scroll state
findings.evidence: The long mobile capture shows a 5,608px feed with no progress indication; the CSS probe found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative scroll progress or scroll-state treatment where it improves orientation.

findings.summary: Transient UI is implemented without semantic overlay primitives
findings.evidence: DOM probes across listing and login found zero dialog, popover, and details elements despite menus and the privacy notice surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover for transient menus/notices with native focus and light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Mobile renders a scaled desktop canvas instead of a mobile layout
findings.evidence: At the requested 360x800 condition, layout metrics exposed a 1,366 CSS-pixel layout viewport scaled to 0.2635 and the screenshot shows extremely small text and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the 1160px body minimum width and create intrinsic mobile layouts that reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Reusable content grids do not respond at component level
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules; mobile behavior relies on a scaled, fixed-width page and viewport-wide rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce size containers for artwork grids, cards, search, and account prompts and adapt them with @container.

findings.summary: Many targets are too small and keyboard focus is not visible
findings.evidence: The live probe counted 193 rendered targets below 24px in at least one dimension; the first focused button computed to outline-style none. Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase targets to at least 24x24 CSS pixels with spacing and add an obvious :focus-visible ring.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are outside good thresholds
findings.evidence: Trace measured LCP 6.98s; Lighthouse lab LCP was 21.0s, TBT 751ms, and CLS 0.111. Artwork layout CLS reached 0.358.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce startup JavaScript, and reserve all media and banner geometry.

findings.summary: Late content causes substantial layout shift
findings.evidence: Layout observers measured CLS 0.205 on listing and 0.358 on artwork, with individual shifts up to 0.223.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image, ad, account-prompt, and async-section space with dimensions or aspect-ratio.

findings.summary: Startup JavaScript blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: Trace found five long tasks and 168ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 751ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, defer non-critical work, and load ad/analytics code after content and interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is slow and script-heavy
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 127 requests and 3.16MB transferred, including 2.84MB of script; trace LCP occurred at 6.98s.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten dependency chains, prioritize the LCP image, and defer scripts that do not contribute to first content.

findings.summary: The page ships an excessive script payload
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 69 script requests and 2.84MB transferred for a public listing, with many ad-tech origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by visible feature and remove, consolidate, or delay third-party bundles.

findings.summary: Controls and links lack accessible names and landmarks
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt, link-name, frame-title, landmark-one-main, and accessibility-tree audits; probe counted 121 unnamed links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable control an accessible name, title frames, provide alt text, and add a main landmark.

findings.summary: Some text fails WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit on the mobile listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Update muted text and control colors to meet WCAG AA in every theme.

findings.summary: Focus and document structure are not robust
findings.evidence: The page has no main element, 121 unnamed links, and the focused button computed outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add semantic landmarks and headings, remove empty links, and implement consistent :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: Scaled mobile rendering makes text illegible
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot fits a 1,366px-wide desktop canvas into the phone viewport, reducing text and controls to a fraction of intended size.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow rather than scale the desktop canvas; use fluid type and comfortable card/grid measures.

findings.summary: Reflow and target sizing fail on mobile
findings.evidence: The narrow capture is a scaled desktop layout and Lighthouse failed target-size; the probe found 193 undersized targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed minimum widths and ensure controls remain usable at 320 CSS pixels and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: Advertising requests generate console errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded CORS failures and failed resource loads from Geniee and Adingo advertising endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct or remove failing ad integrations and contain optional third-party failures.

findings.summary: Images lack dimensions and responsive delivery
findings.evidence: Image audit found 17 of 24 images without dimensions, five oversized, five without srcset, and 21 in legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height, responsive srcset/sizes, and modern-format variants while retaining fallbacks.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and browser lifecycle blockers remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported deprecated Shared Storage, persistent storage, Topics, and Protected Audience use, plus BFCache and inspector-issues failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or remove deprecated third-party integrations and resolve BFCache and DevTools Issues blockers.

findings.summary: Rich pages omit structured entity metadata
findings.evidence: The artwork page has Open Graph metadata, but the live probe found zero JSON-LD blocks on the public content surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org ImageObject or CreativeWork JSON-LD that matches visible artwork and creator data.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: Header audit found no CSP or X-Content-Type-Options; cookie audit found eight cookies without Secure and all 18 with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and nosniff, then set Secure and the narrowest appropriate SameSite value on every cookie.

findings.summary: Public browsing activates a large tracking footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker audit found 34 third-party origins and 12 known tracker domains; multiple analytics identifiers persist for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce tracking to essential, consented vendors, shorten identifier lifetime, and defer analytics until consent/context.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policies are missing
findings.evidence: Headers lacked CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and X-Content-Type-Options; HSTS and X-Frame-Options were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Core listing content is mostly unavailable without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 7% raw/rendered word coverage and classified the listing as a JS shell; artwork coverage was 14%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful artwork cards, links, creator names, and descriptions, then hydrate enhancements.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes
findings.evidence: Image audit found 21 legacy-format images, five oversized images, five without srcset, and 17 without dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP variants sized to their rendered slots and reserve dimensions.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics dominate work
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 69 script requests and tracker audit found 34 third-party origins, while trace recorded repeated long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendors and defer non-essential background work until idle and consented.

findings.summary: Third-party script cost is disproportionate
findings.evidence: The public listing transferred 3.16MB across 127 requests; 2.84MB was script and 34 third-party origins were contacted.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and enforce it before adding or loading advertising vendors.

findings.summary: Machine clients must scrape a JavaScript-heavy interface
findings.evidence: No structured agent capability was exposed, and non-JS discoverability covered only 7% of listing content despite clear search and browsing tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Start with complete semantic server-rendered content and consider narrowly scoped agentic search/bookmark tools with user confirmation.

findings.summary: Repeated feed interaction grows the retained heap
findings.evidence: Heap summary rose from 68.45MB and 1,463,236 nodes to 72.79MB and 1,537,506 nodes after 10 bottom/top scroll cycles, a 6.3% size increase. Separate-load noise limits confidence, but the direction warrants profiling.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile repeated feed scrolling in one persistent session, release off-screen resources/listeners, and verify a plateau after garbage collection.

findings.summary: The public listing has a large baseline heap footprint
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 1,463,236 nodes and 68.45MB self size before prolonged interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial component/object count, unload unused feature modules, and virtualize long result sets.
